title: Proper base change with $\kunZn$-coefficients
statement: Let $n\geq1$ be an integer and put $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism], let $g:Y^{\prime}\to Y$ be any morphism, and form the cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with $X^{\prime}=Y^{\prime}\times_YX$ and projections $f^{\prime}:X^{\prime}\to Y^{\prime}$ and $g^{\prime}:X^{\prime}\to X$. For every $K\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the canonical unbounded exchange morphism [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] $$\Ex_{\square,K}:g^{-1}Rf_*K\longrightarrow Rf^{\prime}_*(g^{\prime})^{-1}K$$ is an isomorphism in $D(Y^{\prime}_{\Et},\Lambda)$. No invertibility assumption on $n$ is imposed.

proof.text: First prove the assertion when $Y$ and $Y^{\prime}$ are quasi-compact. The morphism $f^{\prime}$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Proper morphisms are of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] separately to $f$ and $f^{\prime}$, obtaining bounds $d,d^{\prime}\geq0$ for their ordinary fibre dimensions. Apply [lem-kun-proper-torsion-cd-bound] to conclude that their higher direct images of every torsion abelian sheaf vanish above $2d,2d^{\prime}$, respectively. This uses no finite-type structure over a field.

source.place: Tag 0F0C, lemma-proper-base-change-mod-n, first three sentences (0A3V and 095U)

proof.text: Work in one sufficiently large universe so the small etale sites and coefficient sheaves are small. Their $\Lambda$-module sheaf categories are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck]; the functors $f_*,f^{\prime}_*$ on these categories are additive and left exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact]. Every $\Lambda$-module sheaf is annihilated by $n$, hence has torsion underlying abelian sheaf. Taking cohomology of the comparison $b_u$ of [lem-kun-unbounded-abelian-exchange-comparison] at a sheaf in degree zero identifies its module higher direct images with its abelian higher direct images after forgetting. Exactness and conservativity of forgetting therefore carry the two bounds of step 1 to all module sheaves. Thus [lem-kun-finite-cd-acyclic-complex] applies to $f_*$ and $f^{\prime}_*$.

source.place: Tag 0F0C, lemma-proper-base-change-mod-n, finite cohomological dimension paragraph; coefficient comparison 0D6J(3)

proof.text: Choose a representative of $K$ and a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex $I^{\bullet}$ of $\Lambda$-module sheaves with every $I^r$ injective, by [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence] applied to the Grothendieck category in step 2. By [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], $Rf_*K$ is represented by $f_*I^{\bullet}$; inverse images are exact termwise functors by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. In particular $(g^{\prime})^{-1}I^{\bullet}$ represents $(g^{\prime})^{-1}K$.

source.place: Tag 0F0C, lemma-proper-base-change-mod-n, choice of the degreewise-injective K-injective representative (079P)

proof.text: For each $r$, [lem-sbc-restrict-scalars-injective-direct-image-acyclic] applied to $\mathbf Z\to\Lambda$ gives $R^q f_*(I^r_{ab})=0$ for $q>0$; applied to $\Lambda\to\Lambda$ it also gives module $f_*$-acyclicity of $I^r$. The sheaf $I^r_{ab}$ is torsion. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-torsion-assembly] to it: the canonical abelian sheaf base-change maps $g^{-1}R^qf_*I^r_{ab}\to R^qf^{\prime}_*(g^{\prime})^{-1}I^r_{ab}$ are isomorphisms for all $q$. Therefore $R^qf^{\prime}_*(g^{\prime})^{-1}I^r_{ab}=0$ for $q>0$. Comparison $b_{f^{\prime}}$ in [lem-kun-unbounded-abelian-exchange-comparison], together with its exact conservative forgetting, gives the same vanishing in module sheaves. In degree zero, the same abelian theorem says that the underived sheaf exchange is an isomorphism. The module adjunction has the underlying abelian unit and counit by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Its underived mate $c^r:g^{-1}f_*I^r\to f^{\prime}_*(g^{\prime})^{-1}I^r$ therefore has exactly that underlying abelian exchange, so is an isomorphism: the inverse of a bijective module map is module-linear.

source.place: Tag 0F0C, lemma-proper-base-change-mod-n, usual proper base change on each injective term (095T)

proof.text: Put $L^{\bullet}=(g^{\prime})^{-1}I^{\bullet}$. All its terms are $f^{\prime}_*$-acyclic by step 4. The comparison $\alpha_L:Q(f^{\prime}_*L^{\bullet})\to Rf^{\prime}_*(QL^{\bullet})$ is an isomorphism by [lem-kun-finite-cd-acyclic-complex]. Choose a K-injective replacement $r:L^{\bullet}\to J^{\bullet}$ with injective terms by [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence]. Its terms are $f^{\prime}_*$-acyclic by the identity-coefficient case used in step 4, so $\alpha_J$ is also an isomorphism. Naturality of $\alpha$ gives $Rf^{\prime}_*(Qr)\alpha_L=\alpha_J Q(f^{\prime}_*r)$. Here $Qr$ and both comparisons are isomorphisms, so $Q(f^{\prime}_*r)$ is an isomorphism. This proves the needed computation for the unbounded complex; no unbounded spectral-sequence convergence is presumed.

source.place: Tag 0F0C, lemma-proper-base-change-mod-n, application of 07K7 to the pulled-back complex

proof.text: For clarity identify the canonical arrow, not just its endpoints. The sheaf adjunction of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] defines each $c^r$ as the transpose of $f^{\prime,-1}g^{-1}f_*I^r\xrightarrow{\theta}g^{\prime,-1}f^{-1}f_*I^r\xrightarrow{g^{\prime,-1}\varepsilon_f}L^r$. Naturality in $I^r$ makes these maps a cochain isomorphism $c:g^{-1}f_*I^{\bullet}\to f^{\prime}_*L^{\bullet}$. Its composite $f^{\prime}_*(r)c$ has chain-level transpose $r\,g^{\prime,-1}\varepsilon_f\,\theta$. The right adjoint $f_*$ of the exact $f^{-1}$ preserves K-injective complexes by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], and maps into $I,J,f_*I$ are computed in the homotopy category by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Consequently the chain-level adjunction computes the canonical derived adjunction on these representatives. The displayed transpose is precisely the transpose defining [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] after identifying $K$ with $QI$ and $(g^{\prime})^{-1}K$ with $QJ$ via $Qr$. Uniqueness of adjoint transposes therefore identifies $\Ex_{\square,K}$ with $Q(f^{\prime}_*r)Q(c)$. Step 5 and degreewise invertibility of $c$ show this composite is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0F0C, lemma-proper-base-change-mod-n, final sentence, explicit canonical-mate calculation

proof.text: Remove quasi-compactness as follows. Cover $Y$ by affine opens $V$. For each $V$, cover $g^{-1}(V)$ by affine opens $U$; all the $U$ together cover $Y^{\prime}$. Apply [sbc-lem-etale-locality](2) in the orientation $X_{\mathrm{there}}=Y^{\prime}$, $S_{\mathrm{there}}=Y$, $T_{\mathrm{there}}=X$, with $U_i=U$ and $V_i=V$, to the underlying abelian complex $U_XK$. Each restricted square has proper vertical map by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], and both bases $V,U$ are quasi-compact, so steps 1--6 give its module exchange as an isomorphism. The exchange comparison equation of [lem-kun-unbounded-abelian-exchange-comparison] makes each corresponding abelian exchange an isomorphism. Locality then gives the global abelian exchange as an isomorphism. The same equation and conservativity of forgetting give the original global module exchange as an isomorphism. No quasi-compactness of $g^{-1}(V)$ is needed, since it is covered by the individual affine opens $U$.

tool_uses.why: Uniform ordinary-fibre bound for a finite-type map over a quasi-compact base, the 0A3V input to 0F0C; the unit provides no such bound.
Grothendieck-category resolutions with both K-injectivity and injective terms, the 079P input to 0F0C; used as a homological tool.
Acyclicity after coefficient restriction, used for Z to Lambda and the identity; no smooth-base-change conclusion or route is imported.
Generic additive left-exact constant-coefficient direct image, needed to apply 07K7.
The sheaf-level canonical proper base-change theorem 095T on each injective term, explicitly required by 0F0C; not a replacement for the unit theorem.
Generic exact module inverse image and its adjunction with underlying abelian unit and counit, needed for representatives and the mate calculation.
Generic unbounded canonical-exchange locality 0EZR(2), used to remove quasi-compactness, without invoking smooth base change.
Generic Grothendieckness of module sheaves on a small ringed site, needed for 079P and 07K7.
Generic exact-left-adjoint criterion 08BJ, used to compute the derived adjunction on the chosen representatives.
